full_text_en:
Jintan Construction and Installation Engineering Company v. Daqing Qinglong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project settlement

Ruling Summary

In the trial of a dispute over a construction project construction contract, where the court of first instance, based on the application of the parties, respectively entrusts appraisal institutions to appraise the issues in dispute between the employer and the contractor regarding the total cost of completed works, material analysis price reduction, repair costs for unqualified works, and the like, and after the court of first instance organizes cross-examination, if the parties still object to the appraisal conclusions and appeal, and after supplementary cross-examination in the court of second instance, the parties fail to provide sufficient contrary evidence or rebuttal reasons, the probative force of the appraisal conclusions may be recognized.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 118

Appellant (Plaintiff and Counterclaim Defendant at First Instance): Jintan Construction and Installation Engineering Company, domiciled at No. 669, Jincheng Donghuan Yi Road, Jintan City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Li Lianfu, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Jianyue, lawyer of Beijing Jintai Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant and Counterclaim Plaintiff at First Instance): Daqing Qinglong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 6, Jianshe Street, Development Zone, Daqing City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Shuqing, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Hailong, Deputy General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Luan Zhiqin, lawyer of Harbin Zhongbai Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over construction project settlement between appellant Jintan Construction and Installation Engineering Company (hereinafter referred to as Jintan Company) and appellant Daqing Qinglong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qinglong Company), the Heilongjiang Higher People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2000) Hei Min Chu Zi No. 12 on June 25, 2004, and rendered Civil Ruling (2000) Hei Min Chu Zi No. 12 on October 14, 2004 to amend the judgment. Both Jintan Company and Qinglong Company dissatisfied with the judgment and appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a public hearing on March 3, 2005. Agents ad litem of Jintan Company, Zhu Jianyue, and agents ad litem of Qinglong Company, Liu Hailong and Luan Zhiqin, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

Facts Found by the Court of First Instance

On April 13, 1999, Qinglong Company and Jintan Company entered into a Construction Project Construction Contract. Article 1 of the contract stipulated: Qinglong Company awarded the Daqing Mall Supermarket project (including a 28-story commercial-residential building, a 20-story commercial bank building, and a 4-story podium supermarket) to Jintan Company for construction, with a total floor area of 145,000 square meters; the scope of contract was civil engineering, water and electricity, heating, ventilation, and ancillary works; the method of contract was lump sum for labor and materials; the commencement date was April 20, 1999, and the completion date was December 30, 2001; the quality of the works was to be excellent. Article 6 of the contract stipulated: the contract price was to be implemented in accordance with the current quotas of Daqing City, Heilongjiang Province and the relevant fee collection regulations, and the contract price was to be adjusted based on the actual amount of works performed; the fee standard was to be based on first-class works; temporary facilities were to be provided by Qinglong Company; after the contract was signed, Qinglong Company would pay Jintan Company RMB 4,000,000; when the main structure reached the first floor, 30% would be paid; after the main structure was completed, 25% would be paid; after delivery, 40% would be paid (less the RMB 4,000,000 advance payment); the remaining 5% would be retained as a quality warranty deposit, to be fully paid within one year. If funds were not available on time, thereby affecting the schedule, Qinglong Company would be responsible. Article 7 of the contract stipulated: materials provided by Qinglong Company must be delivered to the site with guaranteed quality and quantity, and acceptance and signing by Jintan Company would serve as the basis for settlement. Article 11 of the contract stipulated: for main materials, where Qinglong Company had the ability to supply, they were to be provided to the construction site at quota prices, and were to be provided on time according to Jintan Company's requirements; delays in schedule due to untimely material supply would be the responsibility of Qinglong Company; the project was to handle all construction approval procedures, with concurrent design and construction; because Qinglong Company had sold the supermarket portion of the project to Harbin Overseas Chinese Economic and Trade Group Corporation, the project could only be delivered in phases; the delivery time for the four floors (podium shopping mall part) was October 30, 1999; to ensure the delivery time, the project must commence on April 15, 1999; if commencement could not be made on April 15, 1999, the schedule would be extended; the RMB 10,000,000 advanced security deposit by Jintan Company would be repaid by Qinglong Company to Jintan Company by October 30, 1999. Qinglong Company would collect and remit all policy-related fees. The construction cost was to be reduced by 9% for high-rise buildings and 8% for podium buildings (excluding planned profit, management fees, and taxes).

On June 8, 1999, the parties entered into an Agreement on Amending the Construction Project Construction Contract Clauses (hereinafter referred to as the Supplementary Agreement), stipulating: Jintan Company would prepare a budget for the actual workload completed each month based on the budget quota of Daqing City, submit it to the supervisory department and the project headquarters by the 25th of each month, and after approval, after deducting the cost of materials supplied by Qinglong Company and machinery and shift costs, 80% of the project payment would be allocated to Jintan Company by the 30th of each month, with 5% retained as a project security deposit, and the balance would be paid to Jintan Company after completion; Jintan Company would not charge for temporary facilities; all materials would be provided by Qinglong Company and settled at the budget quota price of Daqing City; tower cranes and concrete pumps required for the project would be provided by Qinglong Company, and Jintan Company would no longer charge for machinery and machinery shift costs; Qinglong Company would collect and remit all policy-related fees, to be deducted in the final project account.

Qinglong Company obtained the state-owned land use certificate for the disputed project on March 17, 1999, obtained the construction project construction permit on May 21, 1999, and obtained the construction land planning permit on May 24, 1999. Jintan Company was a Class I enterprise for industrial and civil construction.

On November 15, 1999, the Daqing Mall Supermarket project constructed by Jintan Company was completed. At the end of November 1999, when the bank building was constructed to the 15th floor roof, a dispute arose between the parties, and Jintan Company withdrew from the site. Qinglong Company cancelled the 28-story commercial-residential building from the plan, and the actual total floor area of all disputed works was 96,000 square meters, of which the pile foundation was subcontracted by Qinglong Company separately. Qinglong Company had paid Jintan Company RMB 13,352,000 in project payments. Upon reconciliation, the parties confirmed that the price of ancillary works constructed by Jintan Company was RMB 495,000.

On April 16, 2000, the Beijing Branch of Jintan No. 3 Construction and Installation Engineering Company issued a notice of appointment and removal Tan San Jian Jing Zi (2000) No. 3, stating: due to work requirements, after company research and decision, Jing Guoqing was removed as project manager of the Qinglong Company project department and assigned to assist Xu Suoqing in handling the aftermath work with Qinglong Company. On the same day, the Beijing Branch of Jintan No. 3 Construction and Installation Engineering Company issued a letter of appointment Tan San Jian Jing Zi (2000) No. 4, stating: due to work requirements, after company research and decision, Xu Suoqing was appointed as project manager of the Qinglong Company project department, fully authorized to handle the finishing work of the Daqing Qinglong Company (Supermarket Mall) project, including the entire project settlement, payment collection, personnel arrangements, allocation and leasing of materials and machinery, and the undertaking of follow-up projects of Qinglong Company. On January 21, 2001, Xu Suoqing, in the name of Jintan Company, and Qinglong Company formed a settlement statement for the construction labor project undertaken by Jintan Company in 2000, concluding that the cost of civil engineering works completed by Jintan Company in 2000 was RMB 3,074,580.37. In 2000, Xu Suoqing pre-borrowed a total of RMB 7,228,775 in project payments from Qinglong Company.

During the first instance trial, based on the applications of the parties, the court of first instance, on March 13, 2001, April 28, 2001, June 5, 2001, and September 5, 2003, respectively entrusted relevant appraisal institutions to appraise the project cost of the disputed works, the quantity of unqualified works not reported for inspection, the price reduction for material payments, and to preserve evidence.

Jintan Company submitted a written application requesting an appraisal of the construction cost of the Daqing Mall Supermarket project and ancillary works constructed by it. The Judicial Appraisal Center of the Heilongjiang Higher People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Appraisal Center) appraised the construction cost of the Daqing Mall Supermarket project and ancillary works, concluding: (1) The total cost of the Daqing Mall Supermarket and the high-rise works was RMB 56,103,764.68. (2) The total amount for undetermined items was RMB 3,608,045.76, including labor insurance fund of RMB 1,561,292.73 and taxes of RMB 2,046,753.03. For the water and electricity portion, the original appraisal confirmed that 7 cables were completed, while Jintan Company claimed 21 cables were completed. As the appraisal institution could not distinguish the boundary between the 1999 and 2000 construction, it requested the court to investigate and handle the matter. The cost for 7 cables was RMB 208,067.79; the cost for 21 cables was RMB 1,916,565.27. For the ancillary works, as both parties did not provide calculation bases, no appraisal could be conducted.

Qinglong Company submitted a written application requesting an appraisal of the quantity of unqualified works not reported for inspection in the Daqing Mall Supermarket project constructed by Jintan Company, inspection of the completed works on the 4th floor of the Supermarket and the 18th floor of Block B, and preservation of evidence for the unfinished works on the 16th to 21st floors of Lihong New Century, Lihong Famous Stores, and Block B Commercial Bank. The Appraisal Center appraised the quantity of unqualified works not reported for inspection, concluding: "For the 1999 construction works: 1. Unqualified work items confirmed by Qinglong Company and Heilongjiang Hongye Construction Project Supervision Co., Ltd.: interior wall plastering repair cost RMB 169,847.10; fire sprinkler system cost RMB 949,514. 2. Unqualified work items confirmed by Qinglong Company and Heilongjiang Hongye Construction Project Supervision Co., Ltd., repaired by the B Block Project Department of Daqing No. 6 Office of Heilongjiang No. 1 Construction Engineering Company: Supermarket Block B bank floor repair cost RMB 42,810; Supermarket Block B bank wall repair cost RMB 602,408. For the 2000 construction works: 1. Unqualified work items confirmed by Daqing City Construction Quality Supervision Station through on-site inspection, repaired by the B Block Project Department of Daqing No. 6 Office of Heilongjiang No. 1 Construction Engineering Company: repair cost for exterior stone and exterior tiles of Blocks C and D RMB 785,935. 2. Unqualified work items confirmed by Daqing City Construction Quality Supervision Station, repaired by the B Block Project Department of Daqing No. 6 Office of Heilongjiang No. 1 Construction Engineering Company: waterproof repair cost for basements of Blocks A and B RMB 404,232. 3. Unqualified work items confirmed by Jintan Company and Heilongjiang Hongye Construction Project Supervision Co., Ltd., repaired by the B Block Project Department of Daqing No. 6 Office of Heilongjiang No. 1 Construction Engineering Company: ground repair cost for Blocks C and D RMB 527,310; electrical repair cost for Blocks C and D RMB 15,542. 4. Unqualified work items confirmed by Jintan Company and Heilongjiang Hongye Construction Project Supervision Co., Ltd.: plumbing repair cost for Blocks C and D RMB 14,051. 5. Unqualified work items confirmed by Qinglong Company and Heilongjiang Hongye Construction Project Supervision Co., Ltd., repaired by the B Block Project Department of Daqing No. 6 Office of Heilongjiang No. 1 Construction Engineering Company: roof waterproof repair cost for Blocks C and D RMB 325,706; Supermarket Block B bank floor repair cost RMB 142,467."

As the parties could not reach an agreement on the price reduction for materials provided by Qinglong Company to Jintan Company in 1999, they jointly designated Heilongjiang Zhongxin Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. to conduct the analysis for price reduction, concluding: the total price of materials for the civil works portion of Blocks A, C, and D (podium) and Block B high-rise works was RMB 27,614,917.05. According to the contract, the construction cost for high-rise (Block B) was reduced by 9% and for podium (Blocks A, C, D) by 8% (excluding planned profit, management fees, and taxes), resulting in a total material price after reduction of RMB 25,355,275.27. For the water and electricity portion, as both parties did not provide the 1999 Daqing quota standard, the appraisal institution could not appraise this. The unit prices recorded on the bills signed by Jintan Company for the water and electricity materials provided by Qinglong Company to Jintan Company totaled RMB 7,342,506.54.

Jintan Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, alleging: On April 13, 1999, and June 8, 1999, the parties respectively signed the Construction Project Construction Contract and the Supplementary Agreement. The parties agreed: Jintan Company would construct the Daqing Mall Supermarket project for Qinglong Company, with a 8% reduction in construction cost; temporary facilities were to be provided by Qinglong Company; the RMB 10,000,000 advanced by Jintan Company would serve as a project security deposit, to be repaid by Qinglong Company by October 30, 1999; Jintan Company would prepare a budget for the actual workload completed each month based on the budget quota of Daqing City, submit it to the supervisory department and the project headquarters by the 25th of each month, and after approval, after deducting the budget cost of materials provided by Qinglong Company and machinery and shift costs, 80% of the project payment would be allocated to Jintan Company by the 30th of each month. After the contract was signed, Jintan Company completed the civil engineering, plumbing, electrical, fire protection, and other works with guaranteed quality and quantity, and submitted the monthly completed workload to the supervisory department for approval as agreed. The total project payment was RMB 78,720,000. After deducting the materials and machinery usage costs provided by Qinglong Company and the 8% reduction in construction cost, Qinglong Company should pay Jintan Company a project payment of RMB 35,770,000. As agreed, Qinglong Company should pay Jintan Company 80% of the progress payment, i.e., RMB 28,616,000. After deducting the project payment of RMB 11,580,000 already paid by Qinglong Company, an outstanding project payment of RMB 17,036,000 remained. In addition, Qinglong Company refused to return the project security deposit of RMB 10,000,000 and impounded Jintan Company's machinery, equipment, and turnover materials with a total value of RMB 3,000,000. Therefore, Jintan Company requested the court to order Qinglong Company to pay 80% of the progress payment amounting to RMB 17,036,000; return the project security deposit of RMB 10,000,000; pay machinery equipment rental fees and turnover material costs of RMB 3,000,000.

During the first instance trial, Jintan Company amended its claims to: 1. Qinglong Company to pay progress payment of RMB 18,360,000; 2. Qinglong Company to return the project security deposit of RMB 10,000,000; 3. Qinglong Company to return turnover materials and pay rental fees of RMB 1,500,000; 4. Qinglong Company to bear all litigation costs of this case.

After the conclusion of the first instance court debate, Jintan Company further adjusted its claims to: 1. Qinglong Company to pay all project payments and interest for the portion constructed by Jintan Company in 1999 (interest calculated from October 1, 2000, to the date of payment determined by the effective judgment, at the loan interest rate for 1-3 years of the People's Bank of China), and to request priority compensation from the auction proceeds of the project for the above project payments; 2. Qinglong Company to return the loan of RMB 10,000,000 advanced by Jintan Company and pay overdue interest (calculated from November 16, 1999, to the date of payment determined by the effective judgment, at the loan interest rate for 1-3 years of the People's Bank of China); 3. Qinglong Company to return 4,355.56 square meters of steel formwork, 1,066 meters of steel angle formwork, and 19,600 fasteners borrowed.

Qinglong Company responded in defense, arguing that Jintan Company's claims should not be supported. 1. Jintan Company's claim that the total project payment for the civil engineering, plumbing, electrical, and fire protection works completed by it was RMB 78,720,000 was inconsistent with the facts. Based on the actual workload completed by Jintan Company in 1999, Jintan Company was entitled to less than RMB 52,000,000. Qinglong Company had paid RMB 13,350,000 in project payments, supplied materials worth over RMB 50,000,000, and paid living expenses of over RMB 1,000,000. Qinglong Company neither owed progress payments nor any other project payments. 2. Jintan Company breached the contract first. According to the contract, Jintan Company should pay a project security deposit of RMB 30,000,000, but Jintan Company only provided RMB 10,000,000, constituting a breach of the security deposit. Before October 30, 1999, Jintan Company should have delivered the Daqing Mall Supermarket project to Qinglong Company, but Jintan Company failed to complete the works within the specified period, constituting a breach of schedule. The Daqing Mall Supermarket project was a custom-built project for Hualian Company. Due to Jintan Company's breach, the project could not be delivered to the custom builder on time, leading to the rescission of the custom construction contract. Jintan Company should compensate for the losses, and the compensation amount already exceeded the RMB 10,000,000 security deposit provided by Jintan Company. 3. As the construction unit, Jintan Company should provide and lease its own construction equipment. The project payment claimed by Jintan Company already included machinery fees and charges, and Jintan Company's further claim for rental fees from Qinglong Company had no factual or legal basis. The 1999 project was not yet completed, and the contract between the parties had not been rescinded. Jintan Company's claim that Qinglong Company had impounded its turnover materials had no factual basis. Qinglong Company did not respond to the claims adjusted by Jintan Company after the conclusion of the court debate.

Qinglong Company filed a counterclaim, alleging: The parties signed the Construction Project Construction Contract and the Supplementary Agreement, agreeing that the Daqing Mall Supermarket project would be constructed by Jintan Company and should be completed by October 30, 1999. However, the actual construction was carried out by Jintan No. 3 Construction Engineering Company, which lacked the ability to perform the contract, causing direct losses of up to RMB 37,000,000 to Qinglong Company. After deducting the RMB 10,000,000 security deposit provided by Jintan Company, there remained losses of RMB 27,000,000 to be compensated by Jintan Company. As the project had not been completed, some losses could not be calculated at present. Qinglong Company temporarily requested Jintan Company to compensate for losses of RMB 5,000,000. Based on the actual workload completed by Jintan Company in 1999, the project payment should be RMB 52,810,000. Qinglong Company had directly paid project payments of RMB 13,350,000, paid living expenses of RMB 650,000, and provided materials worth RMB 50,390,000. Qinglong Company had actually overpaid project payments of RMB 10,017,000. As the parties had not yet conducted a final account for the disputed project, Qinglong Company requested Jintan Company to return the overpaid project payments of RMB 5,000,000. The costs of the counterclaim were to be borne entirely by Jintan Company.

During the first instance litigation, Qinglong Company added counterclaims: 1. According to the Construction Project Construction Contract, the contract period was from April 15, 1999, to December 30, 2001. Without notifying Qinglong Company, Jintan Company withdrew from the construction site on April 21, 2001, causing huge losses to Qinglong Company. Qinglong Company notified Jintan Company in writing to continue performing the contract, but Jintan Company refused to do so. Therefore, Qinglong Company requested the court to order Jintan Company to continue performing the contract. 2. In November 2000, Jintan Company filed this lawsuit in the court of first instance to demand progress payments. During the court proceedings, Qinglong Company paid Jintan Company a total of RMB 7,228,775 in project payments based on Jintan Company's requests. During this period, the actual project payments Jintan Company was entitled to for the works performed were RMB 3,074,580.37. Qinglong Company actually overpaid project payments of RMB 4,154,194.63. After Jintan Company received the overpaid project payments, it unilaterally withdrew its construction team, making it impossible to perform the contract. Jintan Company should bear compensation liability. Qinglong Company requested Jintan Company to compensate for losses of RMB 5,000,000 caused by the breach of contract. 3. Litigation costs were to be borne by Jintan Company.

Jintan Company responded to Qinglong Company's counterclaim as follows: Qinglong Company's claim for RMB 5 million in damages has no factual basis; Jintan Company performed the construction in accordance with the agreement and did not breach the contract. Whether Qinglong Company overpaid the project funds will become self-evident once the appraisal conclusion of the project cost is made. Qinglong Company's failure to pay the project funds as agreed led to the inability to perform the contract; Jintan Company has the right to suspend construction and rescind the contract. The losses caused by the suspension and rescission shall be borne by Qinglong Company. In summary, Qinglong Company's counterclaim lacks evidence and should not be supported, and the costs of the counterclaim shall be borne by Qinglong Company.

Concerning the disputed issues in the principal claim and the counterclaim, both parties submitted relevant evidence, and the court of first instance organized both parties for cross-examination.

The court of first instance found through trial: (1) Regarding Qinglong Company's assertion that Jintan Company should pay a project performance bond of RMB 30 million, but Jintan Company only paid RMB 10 million and whether the advanced RMB 10 million project performance bond should be returned to Jintan Company. After Jintan Company advanced the RMB 10 million project performance bond, Qinglong Company issued a receipt to Jintan Company "and noted the repayment date as November 25, 1999." Both parties had no objection to the agreement that Jintan Company would advance the RMB 10 million project performance bond. It shall be determined that the advanced RMB 10 million project performance bond was in fact a loan. This loan was not subject to any conditions, so Qinglong Company shall return it.

(2) Regarding the issue of Jintan Company requesting Qinglong Company to pay RMB 1.5 million for machinery and equipment leasing fees and revolving material costs. According to the Supplementary Agreement, the tower cranes and concrete pumps required for the project were to be provided by Qinglong Company, and Jintan Company would no longer charge machinery fees or machinery-shift fees. The parties also agreed that if Jintan Company failed to have construction management technical personnel, workers, scaffolding, iron supports, and steel formwork in place, or failed to bring them to the site in advance as required by the project's needs, thereby affecting the construction schedule, the resulting economic losses would be borne by Jintan Company. Since the parties did not agree that Qinglong Company would pay Jintan Company's machinery and equipment leasing fees and revolving material costs, Jintan Company's claim in this regard is not supported.

(3) Regarding whether Jintan Company's adjusted claims should be tried. Jintan Company adjusted its original claims after the conclusion of the court debate. According to Article 126 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 156 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, after a case is accepted and before the conclusion of the court debate, the additional claims raised by Jintan Company and the counterclaim raised by Qinglong Company may be tried together. However, Jintan Company changed its claims after the court debate concluded, and Qinglong Company raised an objection to this. Therefore, the changed claims shall not be tried.

(4) Regarding whether the construction period should be extended and Qinglong Company's counterclaim for Jintan Company to compensate for losses. According to the Construction Project Construction Contract, the Daqing Mall Supermarket Project must commence on April 15, 1999; if it could not commence, the construction period would be extended. Jintan Company submitted a commencement report signed and sealed by Qinglong Company, indicating the commencement date as May 15, 1999. Qinglong Company objected to this but failed to provide corresponding evidence to verify its objection. Therefore, it shall be determined that the commencement date was May 15, 1999, and the construction period should be extended to November 25, 1999. Jintan Company completed the Daqing Mall Supermarket Project on schedule. Qinglong Company's claim that Jintan Company should bear liability for delayed delivery cannot be supported. Qinglong Company applied for an appraisal of the volume of unverified and non-conforming work performed by Jintan Company. The appraisal concluded that the total cost for rework and repair of the projects built by Jintan Company in 1999 and 2000 was RMB 3,979,822.10. The parties agreed that the project quality grade should be excellent. Although the project was incomplete, Qinglong Company's claim for Jintan Company to pay the costs of rework and repair for the non-conforming quality should be supported. The costs for rework and repair of non-conforming work shall be deducted from the project funds Qinglong Company pays to Jintan Company.

(5) Regarding the issue of policy-related fees collected and paid on behalf of the parties. The parties agreed that Qinglong Company would collect and pay all policy-related fees on behalf of the parties, to be deducted during the final project settlement. Therefore, it shall be determined that the labor insurance fund of RMB 1,561,292.73 and the tax of RMB 2,046,753.03, totaling RMB 3,608,045.76, shall be collected and paid by Qinglong Company on behalf of the parties. Jintan Company should not charge this fee. This fee shall be deducted from the project funds Qinglong Company pays to Jintan Company.

(6) Regarding Qinglong Company's counterclaim for Jintan Company to compensate for losses caused by unilaterally repudiating the contract. Qinglong Company failed to pay Jintan Company the agreed RMB 4 million in project funds and failed to return the RMB 10 million project performance bond advanced by Jintan Company. Qinglong Company was the first to breach the contract. Qinglong Company provided a heating supply agreement signed with Daqing Xincheng Property Management Co., Ltd. and a certificate from the Business Department of Bank of China Daqing Branch, requesting Jintan Company to compensate Qinglong Company for RMB 4.5 million in heating fees for the incomplete project for one year and RMB 6,043,000 in additional interest arising from Qinglong Company's inability to repay bank loans on schedule due to Jintan Company's breach. However, Qinglong Company did not provide a receipt for the payment of heating fees. The heating supply agreement alone does not prove that the heating fees were actually incurred, so this loss is not recognized. The certificate from the Business Department of Bank of China Daqing Branch confirms that Daqing Meigu Building Materials Co., Ltd. paid loan interest of RMB 6,043,000 in 1999-2000, but it does not prove that this was additional interest, nor does it confirm that Qinglong Company was the borrower of this loan. Therefore, Qinglong Company's claim in this regard cannot be supported.

(7) Regarding Qinglong Company's assertion that the 1999 and 2000 projects constructed by Jintan Company should be settled together and that Jintan Company should refund the overpaid project funds of RMB 4,154,194.63. After Jintan Company withdrew from the construction site at the end of November 1999, on April 16, 2000, although Jintan City No. 3 Construction and Installation Engineering Company Beijing Branch issued a notice of appointment and removal, the content of the notice stated that Jing Guoqing was responsible for cooperating with Xu Suoqing in the follow-up work with Qinglong Company, and Xu Suoqing had full authority to be responsible for the finishing work of the project with Qinglong Company (Supermarket Mall). According to this notice of appointment and removal, Jing Guoqing and Xu Suoqing conducted a handover. It shall be determined that Jintan Company acknowledged that Jintan City No. 3 Construction and Installation Engineering Company Beijing Branch would continue the construction, and Xu Suoqing's actions represented Jintan Company. The 2000 labor service project settlement formed by Xu Suoqing in the name of Jintan Company with Qinglong Company shall be recognized. Therefore, in 2000, Xu Suoqing pre-borrowed project funds of RMB 7,228,775 from Qinglong Company. After deducting the labor service fees of RMB 3,074,580.37 that Qinglong Company should pay, Qinglong Company's claim that Jintan Company should refund the overpaid project funds of RMB 4,154,194.63 shall be supported. However, the two-year project should be calculated based on 21 cables. Using the cost of 21 cables, RMB 1,916,565.27, minus the cost of 7 cables, RMB 208,067.79, Qinglong Company shall pay Jintan Company a cable cost of RMB 1,708,497.48.

(8) Regarding whether the materials provided by Qinglong Company to Jintan Company in 1999 should be calculated according to the prevailing Daqing City current quota or the unit price on the supply receipt, and the issue of price deduction. According to the agreement of the parties, for the materials used by Jintan Company for the disputed project drawn from Qinglong Company in 1999, the total cost should be calculated based on the prevailing Daqing City current quota. For the portion of materials exceeding the quota, the total price should be calculated at market prices. Heilongjiang CITIC Accounting Firm Co., Ltd., after appraisal, concluded that the cost of civil engineering materials provided by Qinglong Company to Jintan Company in 1999 should be RMB 25,355,275.27. This conclusion shall be adopted. Regarding the materials for the electrical and plumbing portion, as both parties did not provide the Daqing quota standard for the electrical and plumbing portion in 1999, the appraisal institution could not conduct the appraisal, and the parties could not reach a mutual agreement. Therefore, the cost of the materials for the electrical and plumbing portion provided by Qinglong Company to Jintan Company shall be determined based on the total amount of RMB 7,342,506.54 stated on the receipts acknowledged and signed by Jintan Company. Qinglong Company shall deduct a total material cost of RMB 32,697,781.81 from the project funds payable to Jintan Company. Qinglong Company's assertion that all materials it provided to Jintan Company should be priced and deducted based on the amounts stated on the receipts cannot be supported.

(9) Regarding Qinglong Company's request for Jintan Company to continue performing the contract. After Jintan Company withdrew from the construction site, in June 2001, Qinglong Company subcontracted the unfinished project to a third party, Heilongjiang No. 1 Construction Engineering Company. It is no longer possible for Qinglong Company to request Jintan Company to continue performing the contract. This claim is not supported.

In summary, the Construction Project Construction Contract and the Supplementary Agreement are the true expressions of intent of both parties, do not violate legal provisions, and shall be deemed valid. In accordance with Article 106, Paragraph 1, Article 108, and Article 111 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 269, 275, and 281 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows: (1) The Construction Project Construction Contract signed on April 13, 1999, and the Supplementary Agreement signed on June 8, 1999, between Qinglong Company and Jintan Company are rescinded; (2) Qinglong Company shall return the RMB 10 million project performance bond advanced by Jintan Company; (3) Within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, Qinglong Company shall pay Jintan Company 80% of the project funds of RMB 11,724,014.96, i.e., RMB 9,379,211.97 (total project cost RMB 56,103,764.68 + ancillary project cost RMB 495,000 + labor service fees RMB 3,074,580.37 + cable cost RMB 1,708,497.48 - paid project funds RMB 13,352,000 - material deduction cost RMB 32,697,781.81 - labor insurance fund RMB 1,561,292.73 - tax RMB 2,046,753.03); (4) Within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, Jintan Company shall pay Qinglong Company RMB 3,979,822.10 for project rework and repair costs; (5) Within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, Jintan Company shall refund the overpaid project funds of RMB 4,154,194.63 to Qinglong Company; (6) The other claims of Jintan Company and Qinglong Company are not supported. After calculating the total of items (2), (3), (4), and (5) above, Qinglong Company shall pay Jintan Company RMB 11,245,195.24. The case acceptance fee of RMB 160,160 is to be borne by Jintan Company in the amount of RMB 56,856.80 and by Qinglong Company in the amount of RMB 103,303.20; the counterclaim fee of RMB 85,010 is to be borne by Jintan Company in the amount of RMB 46,075.42 and by Qinglong Company in the amount of RMB 38,934.58; the appraisal fee of RMB 305,000 is to be borne by Jintan Company in the amount of RMB 60,000 and by Qinglong Company in the amount of RMB 245,000; the preservation fee of RMB 20,000 is to be borne by Jintan Company in the amount of RMB 10,000 and by Qinglong Company in the amount of RMB 10,000.

On October 14, 2004, the court of first instance issued a Civil Ruling ( [2000] Hei Min Chu Zi No. 12) to correct a clerical error in the calculation in the original judgment. The details are as follows: (1) The content "3. Within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, Qinglong Company shall pay Jintan Company 80% of the project funds of RMB 11,724,014.96, i.e., RMB 9,379,211.97..." on page 32, lines 5 to 10 of the original judgment is hereby corrected to: "3. Within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, Qinglong Company shall pay Jintan Company project funds of RMB 503,262.02..." (specifically calculated as 80% of RMB 56,103,764.68, etc.); (2) The content "After calculating the total of items 2, 3, 4, and 5 above, Qinglong Company shall pay Jintan Company RMB 11,245,195.24" on page 32, lines 17 to 18 of the original judgment is hereby corrected to: "After calculating the total of items 2, 3, 4, and 5 above, Qinglong Company shall pay Jintan Company RMB 2,369,245.29"; (3) The content regarding the allocation of case acceptance fee, counterclaim fee, appraisal fee, and preservation fee on pages 32-33 is hereby corrected to reflect the new allocation amounts as follows: case acceptance fee RMB 160,160 to be borne by Jintan Company in the amount of RMB 104,104 and by Qinglong Company in the amount of RMB 56,056; counterclaim fee RMB 85,010 to be borne by Jintan Company in the amount of RMB 46,075.42 and by Qinglong Company in the amount of RMB 38,934.58; appraisal fee RMB 305,000 to be borne by Jintan Company in the amount of RMB 167,500 and by Qinglong Company in the amount of RMB 137,500; preservation fee RMB 20,000 to be borne by Jintan Company in the amount of RMB 10,000 and by Qinglong Company in the amount of RMB 10,000.

Both Jintan Company and Qinglong Company were dissatisfied with the judgment and ruling of the first instance and appealed to this court.

Jintan Company appealed, arguing that the judgment and ruling of the first instance contained errors of fact and should be corrected. Main reasons: (1) The court of first instance improperly handled the labor insurance fund and tax. The court of first instance erred by not including the labor insurance fund and tax (totaling RMB 3,608,045.76) in the project cost. Furthermore, without Qinglong Company providing any valid receipts for actual collection and payment, the court deducted RMB 3,608,045.76 from the project cost of RMB 56,103,764.68, which did not include the labor insurance fund and tax, directly resulting in Jintan Company receiving RMB 7,216,091.52 less. (2) The handling of the price deduction for electrical and plumbing materials was unfair. In the 1999 project cost appraisal conclusion, the total cost of the electrical and plumbing portion was RMB 4,478,674.18, calculated by the appraisal institution based on the quota standard as agreed by both parties. The price deduction for electrical and plumbing materials should also follow this quota standard. However, the court of first instance, citing the unavailability of a quota standard for calculation, directly determined the amount based on the RMB 7,342,506.54 stated on the supply receipts, which violates the contract agreement and is also inequitable. (3) The handling of project rework and repair costs was improper. The court of first instance directly used a large amount of invalid evidence and evidence not subject to cross-examination as the basis for calculating rework and repair costs. Jintan Company does not recognize any of these costs except for the RMB 169,847.10 for interior wall plastering rework. (4) The judgment finding that Qinglong Company overpaid project funds was erroneous. Qinglong Company claimed it had overpaid project funds but failed to provide valid evidence. Therefore, the court of first instance's decision to deduct the overpaid project funds of RMB 4,154,194.63 from the amount Qinglong Company should pay Jintan Company has no factual or legal basis. (5) There were errors in the calculation of progress payments for the project. The erroneous calculation method in the first instance led to a significant reduction in the amount Jintan Company should receive in this case. (6) When Jintan Company made its final amendment to its claims, the court debate in the first instance had not yet concluded. The court of first instance's failure to hear the amended claims constituted a procedural violation. Based on this, Jintan Company requests: 1. Apart from upholding Items (1) and (2) of the first instance judgment, to set aside the remaining parts of the first instance judgment and ruling, and to amend the judgment ordering Qinglong Company to pay Jintan Company RMB 26,851,013.89 (including project price of RMB 16,851,013.89 and the performance bond of RMB 10 million) plus corresponding interest. 2. To order Qinglong Company to bear the litigation costs, appraisal fees, preservation fees of the first instance, and the litigation costs of the second instance.

During the second instance trial, Jintan Company explicitly stated that it would abandon its procedural argument raised in the appeal that the court of first instance's failure to support the claims amended before the conclusion of the court debate at first instance constituted a procedural violation.

Qinglong Company appealed, arguing that the first instance did not ascertain Jintan Company's breach of contract, and the judgment's factual findings were unclear and the result erroneous. The main reasons were: (1) The first instance court erred in determining which party, Jintan Company or Qinglong Company, breached the contract. In reality, Qinglong Company fully and beyond the agreed terms performed its contractual obligations, with no breach whatsoever. However, Jintan Company violated the contract by failing to deliver the custom-built project within the agreed period and unilaterally withdrawing from the construction site, thereby constituting a breach and should bear liability for breach. The first instance court ignored the existence of unfinished work and considered that Jintan Company had fully performed the contract, which constituted an unclear factual finding. Not only was the project unfinished, but even the completed parts had major quality hazards requiring rework, and the rework costs were appraised at over RMB 3.9 million. The first instance court failed to identify the above breaches of Jintan Company, and instead considered that Qinglong Company breached first and Jintan Company did not constitute breach, which was manifestly improper. (2) The first instance court's determinations and calculations on several amounts were erroneous and should be corrected. The main issues included: 1. Project progress payments. The first instance court misunderstood Jintan Company's claims. In the complaint filed on September 29, 2000, Jintan Company claimed project progress payments of RMB 17,036,000, and on February 5, 2001, changed the claim to RMB 13.86 million. However, the judgment erroneously determined RMB 18.36 million, which was RMB 4.5 million more than the amount claimed by Jintan Company. 2. Cable costs. Regarding cable costs, whether finally determined as 7 cables or 21 cables, the unit price should be uniform. However, according to the first instance court's determination, the cost for 7 cables was RMB 208,067.79 and for 21 cables was RMB 1,916,565.20. The unit price for 7 cables was RMB 29,732.97, and for 21 cables was RMB 91,265, a difference of RMB 61,542 per unit, totaling RMB 1,293,882 for 21 cables. All materials for the disputed project were provided by Qinglong Company, and only the 7 cables constructed in 1999 should be charged according to the agreed fee standard. In 2000, the parties agreed on a pure labor contract without involving fee issues, and the labor fees for that year had been fully collected by the other party. Therefore, the first instance court's order that Qinglong Company should pay Jintan Company RMB 1,708,497 for cable costs was an erroneous judgment and should be corrected. 3. Regarding the order on labor fees for the civil works portion in 2000. Although the first instance court's determination that the 2000 labor fees were RMB 3,074,586.37 was correct, under the circumstances where Jintan Company had already overdrawn RMB 4,154,194.63, ordering Qinglong Company to pay an additional RMB 3,074,586.37 to Jintan Company was clearly erroneous. 4. Regarding the 43 withdrawals of living expenses totaling RMB 653,085 by Jintan Company from Qinglong Company and the offset with two vehicles. Jintan Company had acknowledged this, and the first instance judgment's failure to support it was incorrect. 5. The issue of utility fees for the project paid by Qinglong Company. Such fees should reasonably be borne by Jintan Company, and the first instance court's failure to recognize this was an erroneous judgment. 6. In determining the material costs, the first instance only adopted the appraisal conclusion which had obvious errors, determining the material costs as RMB 32 million, which was even less than the amount admitted by the opposing party. 7. The issue of winter construction fees. The appraisal institution appraised the 1999 winter construction fees at RMB 850,000, and the first instance court's adoption of this lacked evidence. 8. The issue of heating fees and overdue bank loan interest. The heating fees had actually been incurred, but the first instance court erroneously refused to support on the sole ground that there was no receipt. Furthermore, due to Jintan Company's breach, Qinglong Company incurred additional overdue bank loan interest, which should be borne by Jintan Company. The first instance court's refusal to support on the ground that the additional interest was not specified lacked basis. (3) The disputed project in this case was a large-scale construction project, and the cost appraisal should reasonably have been conducted by an appraisal institution with Class A qualifications for construction cost consulting. However, the appraisal institution commissioned by the first instance court only had Class B qualifications for such business scope and was fundamentally unqualified to appraise the disputed project. The first instance court's adoption of the appraisal conclusion from this institution that exceeded its qualification level led to errors in determining the total construction cost for 1999, material costs, and other issues. Therefore, Qinglong Company requested: 1. Reversal of the first instance judgment; 2. Dismissal of Jintan Company's claims; 3. Support of Qinglong Company's counterclaims raised in the first instance; 4. Case acceptance fees to be borne by Jintan Company.

During the second instance trial, Qinglong Company had requested in its appeal that Jintan Company continue to perform the contract, but later clearly stated that because the first instance litigation began in 2000 and the disputed project was later constructed by a third party outside the case and had been delivered for use, this request had become meaningless and was abandoned.

Additionally, when appealing, Qinglong Company argued that the first instance court erred in failing to determine the issue of Jintan Company's 43 withdrawals of living expenses totaling RMB 653,085 from Qinglong Company and the offset with two vehicles. Later, Qinglong Company acknowledged that the first instance judgment had already determined and supported Qinglong Company on this issue, and therefore no longer raised a claim on this matter.

This Court finds through trial: Qinglong Company provided the originals of the corresponding evidence, proving that in 2000, Xu Suoqing had indeed pre-borrowed project funds of RMB 7,228,775 from Qinglong Company. Jintan Company acknowledged the authenticity of the above originals.

It was also found that after the appraisal institution appraised the 1999 construction cost during the first instance, it has so far failed to return the originals of some materials provided by Jintan Company for the appraisal.

It was further found that the unit price difference between the cost of 7 cables and the cost of 21 cables was due to different cable specifications, not a calculation error by the appraisal institution.

It was also found that during the first instance, upon party application, the first instance court commissioned appraisals on the 1999 construction cost, material analysis and price deductions, and quantities of unverified substandard works. All three appraisals were entrusted by the Appraisal Center to external appraisal institutions, and all appraisal conclusions were ultimately jointly issued by the Appraisal Center and the relevant appraisal institution in both names. Heilongjiang Zhonglong Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhonglong Company), which was responsible for appraising the 1999 construction cost, had Class B qualifications for construction cost consulting within its business scope.

It was further found that on February 5, 2001, Jintan Company submitted a written request to change its claims, amending the amount of project progress payments to RMB 18.36 million, not RMB 13.86 million.

Other facts found by this Court are the same as those found by the first instance court.

This Court holds that the "Construction Project Construction Contract" and the "Supplementary Agreement" signed by the parties reflected genuine intentions and are legal and valid. Since the contract could no longer be performed, the first instance court's judgment to terminate the contract was correct. Given that Jintan Company sued in the first instance claiming the project progress payments due for 1999, and Qinglong Company counterclaimed that it had overpaid project funds for 2000 and that the works completed by Jintan Company in both 1999 and 2000 had quality defects requiring rework, and sought compensation for losses caused by Jintan Company's breach, it was not improper for the first instance court to handle the works for both 1999 and 2000 together.

The focus of dispute between the parties mainly centered on several aspects: whether the RMB 10 million project guarantee deposit advanced by Jintan Company should be refunded; how to determine the amount of project progress payments due to Jintan Company; the amount that Qinglong Company could deduct from the project funds; which party, Jintan Company or Qinglong Company, breached the contract; and whether compensation for losses should be paid.

(A) Regarding whether the RMB 10 million project guarantee deposit advanced by Jintan Company should be refunded.

Qinglong Company argued that this RMB 10 million was a project guarantee deposit. Since problems arose with the project, it should be deducted from this amount. The first instance judgment's characterization of it as a loan and ordering Qinglong Company to refund it was incorrect. The first instance court had already found that although the parties agreed that the RMB 10 million was a guarantee deposit, based on the content of the written receipt issued by Qinglong Company to Jintan Company, this RMB 10 million was in fact a loan from Jintan Company to Qinglong Company. Qinglong Company made an unconditional promise regarding the repayment period. Now that the repayment period had expired, Jintan Company's request for refund should be supported. Therefore, the first instance court's characterization of it as a loan and ordering Qinglong Company to refund it was not improper.

(B) Regarding how to determine the amount of project progress payments due to Jintan Company.

The quantities of work completed by Jintan Company can be divided into two parts by time: the work completed in 1999 and the work completed in 2000. Among these, the work completed in 1999 includes the ancillary works of RMB 495,000 which were not appraised but acknowledged by both parties, and the Daqing Shopping Mall Supermarket and high-rise building cost of RMB 56,103,764.68 as appraised. The project funds due to Jintan Company for 1999 were to be calculated according to the fixed rate standard as agreed in the "Construction Project Construction Contract" and the "Supplementary Agreement" between the parties. In this case, Jintan Company requested that Qinglong Company pay project progress payments as agreed, i.e., 80% of the total project funds for 1999. The project funds due to Jintan Company for 2000, under the oral pure labor agreement between the parties, were only labor fees. There was no explicit agreement between the parties regarding payment of labor fees based on progress. Moreover, Qinglong Company had fully paid all labor fees for 2000. Therefore, it was unnecessary to determine the project funds due to Jintan Company for 2000 based on progress.

1. Regarding the project progress payments due to Jintan Company for 1999. The work completed by Jintan Company in 1999 included the ancillary works and the Daqing Shopping Mall Supermarket and high-rise building. The cost of the ancillary works was RMB 495,000, and the cost of the Daqing Shopping Mall Supermarket and high-rise building was RMB 56,103,764.68. The main issues were:

(1) Regarding the cost of the ancillary works. The ancillary works were part of the overall project for 1999. Although not appraised, both parties acknowledged that the cost of the ancillary works was RMB 495,000. According to Jintan Company's claim for 80% project progress payments, the ancillary works, as part of the 1999 project, should also have project progress payments calculated according to the parties' agreement. The first instance judgment only calculated progress payments for the appraised main works (Daqing Shopping Mall Supermarket and high-rise building) according to the agreement, but recognized the ancillary works at 100%, which was inconsistent with the facts and the parties' requests and should be adjusted.

(2) Regarding how to determine the price of materials used in the project. Qinglong Company argued that Jintan Company's signature on the material supply sheets constituted acknowledgment of the prices, quantities, etc. stated therein, and was a change to the agreed term that raw materials would be priced according to the fixed rate. Therefore, the total material cost should be calculated based on the material supply sheets signed by both parties. Moreover, during the first instance trial, Jintan Company admitted to receiving civil works materials totaling RMB 36 million, which was higher than the appraisal conclusion of RMB 32 million. The judgment should not simply adopt the appraisal conclusion without further consideration. Jintan Company argued that the parties had explicitly agreed to calculate material prices according to the fixed rate, and no change was made later. The material supply sheets only evidenced the delivery of material quantities and could not be used to determine material prices. The parties had different views on material prices. Jintan Company's position was consistent with the parties' agreement and should be adopted. Although Jintan Company had indicated during the first instance trial that it had received materials worth RMB 36 million, it also stated at the same time that it was willing to resolve the material issue through appraisal. Since Qinglong Company also agreed to have the construction cost appraised according to the agreed fixed rate standard, this meant that absent sufficient evidence to overturn the appraisal conclusion, it was proper for the first instance judgment to adopt the appraisal conclusion.

Additionally, Qinglong Company argued that the agreed downward adjustment of the construction cost did not include the downward adjustment of material prices, and the first instance judgment's determination that material prices were adjusted downward harmed Qinglong Company's legitimate rights and interests. The parties agreed that after deducting planned profit, management fees, and taxes, the construction cost for the high-rise building would be adjusted downward by 9%, and for the podium by 8%. Since the items deducted before the downward adjustment of the construction cost as agreed by the parties did not include material costs, and material costs are an important component of the construction cost, the overall downward adjustment of the construction cost should also apply to material prices. The first instance court's adoption of the downward-adjusted material prices for the material price deduction analysis was correct.

(3) Regarding the qualification of the appraisal institution. Qinglong Company appealed, arguing that Zhonglong Company, commissioned by the first instance court to appraise the 1999 construction cost, had only Class B qualifications for construction cost consulting within its business scope, while this case involved a large-scale construction project that should have been appraised by an institution with Class A qualifications. Therefore, Qinglong Company contended that the first instance court's adoption of the conclusion from this appraisal institution constituted procedural illegality and applied for a new appraisal. Although Zhonglong Company had Class B qualifications for construction cost consulting, the appraisal institution had been recognized by the relevant local authorities as having the qualification to conduct judicial appraisals, and the appraisal conclusion was not independently completed by Zhonglong Company but was jointly issued by the Appraisal Center and Zhonglong Company. The first instance court's adoption of it was not improper and did not constitute procedural illegality. Qinglong Company did not raise any objection regarding the qualification of the appraisal institution during the first instance. Raising it now during the second instance, and given that the originals of some materials needed for the appraisal could no longer be provided, the conditions for a new appraisal were not met. Therefore, Qinglong Company's request on this matter was not supported.

(4) Regarding the appraisal conclusion for the 1999 construction cost. Upon party application, the Appraisal Center and Zhonglong Company jointly appraised the construction cost of the Daqing Shopping Mall Supermarket project, concluding that the total construction cost of the Daqing Shopping Mall Supermarket and high-rise building was RMB 56,103,764.68, with pending amounts totaling RMB 3,608,045.76 (including labor insurance fund of RMB 1,561,292.73 and taxes of RMB 2,046,753.03). Jintan Company argued that the first instance judgment's determination of the construction cost at RMB 56,103,764.68 did not include the labor insurance fund and taxes, which was inconsistent with industry practice and understated the project funds due to Jintan Company, and should be adjusted. The labor insurance fund and taxes are amounts that the construction unit should pay to the relevant authorities based on its operating income according to the prescribed proportion. The construction cost calculated by the appraisal institution based on the parties' agreement to charge according to the fixed rate already included the parties' profit, taxes and fees, etc., but was not separately listed. Therefore, Jintan Company's claim that the above two items should be added to the construction cost of RMB 56,103,764.68 was not supported by law.

Qinglong Company appealed, arguing that the appraisal conclusion's determination of winter construction fees at RMB 850,000 was erroneous, when the actual amount should be only RMB 58,000. This issue had been explicitly raised by Qinglong Company during the first instance when the first instance court organized the appraisal institution to answer questions on the appraisal conclusion. The appraisal institution responded that the winter construction fees were actually incurred, based on the parties' supervision summaries and the actual situation, and there was no calculation error. Since Qinglong Company now raised the objection without new reasons or evidence, it was not supported by law.

Qinglong Company argued that on February 5, 2001, Jintan Company changed its claim to project progress payments of RMB 13.86 million, but the first instance judgment determined it as RMB 18.36 million, which was RMB 4.5 million more than the amount claimed by Jintan Company. Upon trial by the second instance court, it was found that the written materials for Jintan Company's change of claims on February 5, 2001 were consistent with the first instance judgment, and the project progress payments amount was RMB 18.36 million. Qinglong Company's claim was inconsistent with the facts and was not supported.

Furthermore, Qinglong Company appealed, arguing that the utility fees for the project paid by Qinglong Company should be borne by Jintan Company, and the first instance court's failure to recognize this was an erroneous judgment. In its first instance defense and counterclaim requests and reasons, Qinglong Company did not clearly mention the issue of utility fees paid on behalf of Jintan Company, nor did it submit any specific evidence to the first instance court proving that the utility fees were actually incurred and should be borne by Jintan Company. Now, during the second instance, Qinglong Company raised this issue without providing sufficient evidence, so it was not supported by law.

2. Regarding the labor fees due to Jintan Company for 2000. Qinglong Company argued that the first instance judgment erred in ordering Qinglong Company to pay labor fees of RMB 3,074,586.37 for 2000 when calculating the project funds due to Jintan Company, and this should be corrected. The first instance court had already found that the labor fees due to Jintan Company for 2000 were RMB 3,074,586.37, and Qinglong Company had fully paid that amount. Under this premise, the first instance court, on the one hand, included this amount when determining the project funds due to Jintan Company, and on the other hand, failed to deduct this actually paid amount when calculating Qinglong Company's deductions from the project funds, causing Qinglong Company to bear the 2000 labor fees of RMB 3,074,586.37 twice. Qinglong Company's request on this matter was justified and should be supported. However, the labor fees for 2000 as determined by the first instance judgment were RMB 3,074,580.37, not the RMB 3,074,586.37 as stated in Qinglong Company's appeal.

3. Regarding the cable cost issue. The appraisal conclusion for the 1999 Daqing Shopping Mall Supermarket and high-rise building construction cost of RMB 56,103,764.68 included the cost of 7 cables at RMB 208,067.79. Jintan Company argued that a total of 21 cables were completed in 1999. Qinglong Company argued that only 7 cables were completed in 1999, and the remaining 14 cables were completed in 2000. The appraisal institution could not distinguish the construction boundaries between 1999 and 2000 and requested the court to investigate and determine. The first instance court held that regardless of when the cables were constructed, since they were all constructed by Jintan Company, it ordered Qinglong Company to pay Jintan Company RMB 1,708,497.48, which was the difference between the cost of 21 cables at RMB 1,916,565.27 and the cost of 7 cables at RMB 208,067.79. Qinglong Company argued that in 2000, the other party only earned labor fees and should not be charged according to the fixed rate, and that the project funds for 2000 had been fully paid by Qinglong Company. Therefore, the 14 cables should not be recognized. Additionally, the unit price of the 7 cables was not uniform with that of the 21 cables, indicating an error in the first instance judgment's calculation. During the second instance, it was found that the unit price difference between the 7 cables and the 21 cables was due to different cable specifications, not a calculation error. Qinglong Company's claim that there was a calculation error in the first instance judgment regarding cable costs was unfounded. However, since the 1999 project involved charging according to the fixed rate, and the 2000 work was only for labor fees which had been fully settled, and the parties had different views on the cable issue and neither could provide sufficient evidence to prove their respective positions, the first instance court's approach of determining that all disputed cable costs should be paid by Qinglong Company to Jintan Company calculated according to the fixed rate standard was inappropriate. Qinglong Company's objection on this issue had some merit and should be given appropriate support. Except for the 7 cables that both parties agreed were constructed in 1999, the costs of the disputed 14 cables totaling RMB 1,708,497.48 should be shared between the parties for the adverse consequences. It was determined that Qinglong Company should pay Jintan Company RMB 854,248.74, i.e., 50% of the costs of the 14 disputed cables of RMB 1,708,497.48.

(C) Regarding which party, Jintan Company or Qinglong Company, breached the contract and whether compensation for losses should be paid.

The trial court found that both parties had breached the contract. Although Jintan Company was not in default of the deadline for delivering the Daqing Mall Supermarket Project, its conduct of withdrawing from the construction site without authorization and failing to complete the project in accordance with the agreed quality standards constituted a breach of contract. Qinglong Company's failure to pay the project funds in the agreed amount and within the agreed time limit, and its failure to return the advanced funds as agreed, also violated the parties' agreement.

Qinglong Company argued that Jintan Company breached the agreement to deliver the fixed-construction project before October 30, 1999, and that the actual delivery time was November 25, 1999, thus constituting a default in the construction period, and that the trial court's finding was erroneous. The commencement report jointly signed and acknowledged by both parties indicated that the commencement date was May 15, 1999. Combined with the parties' agreement that if the commencement date was postponed, the completion date would be correspondingly postponed, the postponed completion date should be November 25, 1999. Jintan Company actually completed the project on November 15, 1999. Therefore, the trial court's conclusion that the project was completed on time and that Jintan Company was not in default was correct.

Qinglong Company argued that it had fully performed its contractual obligations, even exceeding the agreed terms, without any breach of contract, and that Jintan Company had breached the contract by failing to complete the project in accordance with the agreed quality standards, among other things. Based on the facts found by the courts of first and second instance, the construction work performed by Jintan Company did not meet the agreed quality grade, there were unqualified works that had not been inspected and accepted, and Jintan Company withdrew from the construction site without authorization. Qinglong Company failed to pay the project funds in the agreed amount and within the agreed time limit, and also failed to return the advanced funds as agreed. Therefore, the trial court's conclusion that both parties had breached the contract was not improper.

Qinglong Company argued that due to the other party's breach, it suffered losses totaling tens of millions of yuan, including heating costs of RMB 4,500,000 for one year for the unfinished project and additional interest of RMB 6,043,000, and that the other party should compensate it for these losses. The trial court's failure to support this claim was incorrect. Regarding the heating cost issue, the trial court found that relying solely on the heating agreement signed by Qinglong Company and Daqing Xincheng Property Management Co., Ltd. was insufficient to establish that the parties had actually performed their rights and obligations under the heating agreement, including payment. Moreover, Qinglong Company failed to provide valid and effective evidence that it had actually paid the amount. Therefore, its claim that it suffered such losses due to the other party's breach could not be supported. Regarding the issue of additional loan interest, Qinglong Company provided a certificate from the Business Department of Bank of China, Daqing Branch, seeking to prove that it had incurred additional interest of RMB 6,043,000 due to its inability to repay bank loans on time. Upon investigation by the trial court and this court, the subject of that loan was not Qinglong Company, and there was no evidence to prove that the funds were indeed used by Qinglong Company. Therefore, the trial court's decision not to support this claim was correct.

In its claim at first instance, Jintan Company requested an order for the other party to pay project progress payments of RMB 18,360,000 and a guarantee deposit of RMB 10,000,000. At the second instance, it added a claim for payment of corresponding interest on the aforementioned two amounts. Because Qinglong Company refused mediation, this court will not hear the new claims added by Jintan Company at the second instance in accordance with the law.

(4) Regarding the scope of items for which Qinglong Company may deduct from the project funds.

Regarding which items Qinglong Company could deduct from the project funds, apart from the RMB 13,352,000 in project funds that Qinglong Company had paid in 1999, which was confirmed by both parties after verification and was therefore deductible, the parties disagreed on whether the following amounts should be deducted from the project funds and how the deduction should be made:

1. The issue of material price rebates. The parties' Supplementary Agreement stipulated that all materials would be provided by Qinglong Company. Therefore, when calculating the project funds that Jintan Company was entitled to receive for the 1999 Daqing Mall Supermarket Project, the cost of civil construction materials and electrical materials had to be deducted from the total project cost. At the request of the parties, the trial court commissioned an appraisal institution to conduct a material price rebate analysis. The conclusion was that the cost of civil construction materials was RMB 25,355,275.27. The cost of electrical materials could not be appraised due to the lack of a quota standard, but it was found that the amount stated on the electrical material supply vouchers signed and acknowledged by both parties was RMB 7,342,506.54. Regarding the price rebate for civil construction materials, the trial court adopted the appraisal conclusion of RMB 25,355,275.27. Although Qinglong Company objected, it failed to provide sufficient evidence to overturn the original appraisal conclusion, so its claim on this point was not supported. Regarding the electrical materials, because neither party provided the contractual quota standard, no appraisal could be made. The trial court ruled that the settlement should be based on the actual amounts on the supply vouchers signed and acknowledged by both parties, and ordered that the price rebate for electrical materials be set at RMB 7,342,506.54. Jintan Company argued that the electrical portion of the 1999 project cost appraisal conclusion was RMB 4,478,674.18, which was calculated by the appraisal institution based on the quota standard agreed upon by the parties. The trial court, when calculating the project funds Jintan Company was entitled to receive, recognized the electrical portion as RMB 4,478,674.18 based on the quota standard. However, when calculating the deduction of project funds by Qinglong Company for the materials it supplied, it recognized the amount as RMB 7,342,506.54 based on the supply vouchers, which was far higher than the quota standard. This was unfair. The price rebate for electrical materials should not exceed the upper limit of RMB 4,478,674.18. Although Qinglong Company argued that the materials requisitioned by the other party were not entirely used for the disputed project and that the rebate should be settled based on actual usage, it failed to provide this court with sufficient evidence to prove its claim. Therefore, Jintan Company's request on this point was well-founded. The price rebate for electrical materials should be RMB 4,478,674.18. The total price rebate for civil construction materials and electrical materials combined should be RMB 29,833,949.45.

2. The issue of the overpayment of project funds of RMB 4,154,194.63 in 2000. Jintan Company argued that it had only undertaken the 1999 project, and that the construction work, borrowing, etc., in 2000 were personal acts of Xu Suoqing and were unrelated to Jintan Company. The trial court had already found and determined that Xu Suoqing succeeded the original project manager, Jing Guoqing, and represented Jintan Company in settling accounts with Qinglong Company, continuing construction, etc. Therefore, Jintan Company's denial that Xu Suoqing's acts were on behalf of Jintan Company was without merit. In 2000, Qinglong Company paid a total of RMB 7,228,775 in project funds to the other party, while the actual total cost of civil construction work completed by Jintan Company was RMB 3,074,580.37. It could therefore be determined that Qinglong Company overpaid project funds by RMB 4,154,194.63 in 2000, and this amount could be used to offset the project funds payable to Jintan Company.

3. The issue of repair and maintenance costs of RMB 3,979,822.10. The parties agreed that the project quality should be excellent. Although a dispute arose between the parties before the project was completed, Jintan Company was still liable to bear the repair and maintenance costs for the unqualified works it had completed that had not been inspected and accepted. The appraisal determined the repair and maintenance costs to be RMB 3,979,822.10. Jintan Company, while acknowledging only a small portion of this amount, argued that the appraisal institution had based its determination on a large amount of materials that had not been authenticated, and that the conclusion should not be adopted. During the first instance, the appraisal institution stated in its explanatory materials that some materials had not been authenticated because Jintan Company itself had refused to fulfill its obligation to authenticate the materials used for the appraisal. Therefore, Jintan Company's reason for not accepting the appraisal conclusion was without merit. The quality of Jintan Company's construction work was substandard, violating the contract. The trial court's decision to support Qinglong Company's claim that Jintan Company should bear the repair and maintenance costs was not improper.

4. The issue of the labor insurance fund of RMB 1,561,292.73 and the tax of RMB 2,046,753.03 collected and remitted on behalf. Jintan Company argued that, in the absence of any evidence from Qinglong Company that it had actually remitted the above amounts, the trial court was wrong to deduct a total of RMB 3,608,045.76 for these two items from the project cost of RMB 56,103,764.68, which did not include these costs, and that this should be corrected. As a construction enterprise, Jintan Company was obligated to pay labor insurance funds and taxes in accordance with relevant regulations after undertaking the project. Whether or not these items were explicitly and separately listed in the project cost did not affect Jintan Company's obligation to pay them. Therefore, Jintan Company's argument that the trial court's order that it bear these costs was improper, on the grounds that the project cost did not include these items, was without merit. Because the parties agreed that Qinglong Company would collect and remit all policy-related fees on behalf of Jintan Company and deduct them in the final settlement, and since Jintan Company's claim in this case was limited to requesting Qinglong Company to pay 80% of the project progress payments, with the remaining 20% of the project funds not yet settled, and because Qinglong Company was at all times unable to prove during the first and second instances that it had actually paid the labor insurance funds and taxes to the relevant authorities, Qinglong Company could, after actually making such payments, correspondingly deduct them from the remaining 20% of the project funds it owes Jintan Company. Jintan Company's claim on this point was reasonable. Therefore, the relevant part of the trial court's judgment, which ordered that these costs be deducted from the project funds payable to Jintan Company and collected and remitted by Qinglong Company, is hereby adjusted.

In summary, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraphs (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Items 1, 2, 4, and 5 of the Civil Judgment (2000) Hei Min Chu Zi No. 12 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court are affirmed.

2. Item 6 of the Civil Judgment (2000) Hei Min Chu Zi No. 12 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court is reversed.

3. Item 3 of the Civil Judgment (2000) Hei Min Chu Zi No. 12 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court is amended to read: Within thirty days after this judgment takes effect, Daqing Qinglong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall pay to Jintan Construction and Installation Engineering Company project progress payments in the amount of RMB 45,279,011.74; Daqing Qinglong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall pay to Jintan Construction and Installation Engineering Company cable project costs in the amount of RMB 854,248.74; when Daqing Qinglong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. makes the aforementioned payments to Jintan Construction and Installation Engineering Company, it shall deduct the already paid project funds of RMB 13,352,000 and the material price rebate of RMB 29,833,949.45, totaling RMB 43,185,949.45.

4. The other appellate claims of Daqing Qinglong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Jintan Construction and Installation Engineering Company are dismissed.

After calculating Items 1 and 3 above, Daqing Qinglong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall pay Jintan Construction and Installation Engineering Company a total of RMB 4,813,294.30.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance, the counterclaim fee, the property preservation fee, and the appraisal fee shall be enforced in accordance with the corrected judgment of the first instance. The court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 245,170, of which Jintan Construction and Installation Engineering Company shall bear RMB 98,068 and Daqing Qinglong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 147,102.

This judgment is final.
